evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep jumps directly into probing: 'Do you have any questions or concerns that I can answer for you right now?' — no time-boxed framing or promise of a dependable quote before asking the customer to engage.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Asked only after extensive probing: 'No, just wanted to give more clarification on what I need' — the customer's need was already being unpacked when the explicit ask for concerns happened.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer raises concern about truck parking at apartment complex ('I don't know if a big truck can go there'). Rep acknowledges but does not dig deeper — customer offers to clarify with building management, rep simply says 'Okay, perfect' and moves forward.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Covered: property type (apartment), floor (second), address, elevator availability, pod location/size, items being moved (60-70% of contents, dining furniture). Not clearly covered: number of rooms in destination apartment, walking distance to building entrance, special items beyond dining table.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Range given ($500–600 for 2.5–3.5 hours at $202/hr) but not personalized to this customer's stated concerns (truck access uncertainty, pod-to-apartment logistics, time window constraints).
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Hourly rate and included services mentioned ('two movers, travel, removing items from pod, insurance, taxes all included'). No mention of trip fee (though rep does reference it existing for other branches), no mention of 15-minute increments or 2.5-hour minimum commitment language, no deposit/cancellation fee clarity until customer asks.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Never asked. Rep moves directly from pricing to 'Can you send me a quote?' without gauging customer reaction to the estimate.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: No. The Two Promises section is entirely skipped.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Not asked. Rep moves to sending email without checking what remaining concerns exist.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Never made. Rep offers to send an email quote but does not ask 'Would you like our help with your move?' — instead customer drives the close by requesting email and rep complies.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Partial. Date (Monday, October 5th) and arrival window (around 9:00 AM, settled from original 8:00–8:30 AM availability) confirmed. Phone number, final arrival window, crew size, and crew notes about customer concerns are NOT confirmed. Email is sent, but rep does not confirm receipt or walk through booking details.

top_strength: Rep gathered complete discovery basics (name, moving day, route, approximate volume) and discovered a nuanced logistics situation (pod-to-apartment partial load with specific time constraints), then found an alternative time slot to accommodate the customer's 9 AM pickup window.
coaching_note: Section 1 must always include the quid pro quo framing (time-boxed ask + promise of a dependable quote + wait for yes) before probing; Section 2's Their Agenda must come before you start asking logistics details; and Sections 4–7 (estimate, Two Promises, final concerns, and explicit ask for the business) are missing entirely — the call ends without a clear close or commitment, just an email being sent.
